name: Philips L Prize white LED lighting lamp
description: A screw-base solid-state lamp using LEDs and phosphor to provide white general illumination.

impact.note: One lamp model among early LED replacement bulbs; an efficient substitute for buyers in one market, with no clear dependence of later lamps on it.

date.label: 3 August 2011
date.basis: Date stated in the 2012 DOE program update.

events.statement: Philips was announced as winner of the L Prize for a 60-watt replacement LED lamp.
events.caveats: Recognition of the tested lamp is not evidence of general retail availability at this date; the final production design could differ.

evidence.supports: The May 2012 DOE update dates the award announcement to 3 August 2011.

date.label: by 23 May 2012
date.basis: A DOE update dated 23 May 2012 reports these figures. The FAQ refers to an 18 January 2012 webinar, but its own issue date is not explicit.

events.statement: DOE materials describe approximately 940 lumens and 94 lumens per watt for the Philips L Prize lamp.
events.caveats: The FAQ recaps a webinar held on 18 January 2012; this does not independently establish its exact publication date. The figures describe the lamp reported by DOE, not an average across all LED bulbs.

evidence.supports: The Q&A recap of the 18 January 2012 webinar reports approximately 940 lumens and 94 lm/W.
The May 2012 update reports 940 lumens and 94 lm/W for the L Prize lamp.

date.basis: Date in the cited source; see scope and caveats.

events.statement: Philips began selling the L Prize lamp online in February 2012.

evidence.supports: A litigant’s 2017 complaint states the dates for online and retail sales of the lamp.
DOE reports approximately 940 lumens and 94 lm/W for the specific lamp.

events.caveats: A particular white-light lamp, not the first white LED or first commercial LED bulb. The sales chronology is stated in a later litigant’s complaint, not a judicial finding.

evidence.supports: The 2017 complaint attributes online and retail sales of the lamp to Philips.

date.basis: Date in the cited source; see scope and caveats.

events.statement: The lamp entered retail stores on 22 April 2012, according to a later litigant’s complaint.

evidence.supports: A litigant’s 2017 complaint states the dates for online and retail sales of the lamp.

events.caveats: Sale is availability, not a count of buyers or installations. The sales chronology is stated in a later litigant’s complaint, not a judicial finding.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated award establishes this tested lamp by August 2011; subsequent product availability is recorded separately.

research.note: Independent reader checked the DOE product figures and the 2017 complaint’s attributed sales chronology; the complaint is not a judicial decision. No asserted link to the specific Nichia emitter. Award and bounded measurement-report events added after independent review; the date in the FAQ identifies the webinar, not necessarily issuance.

measures.conditions: Approximate DOE-reported product output in materials associated with the January 2012 webinar and in a May 2012 update; not an independently sampled market average.
